eli5.text: The system's record of which database update to run at a particular step was pointing at the wrong file, so the update mechanism could not match it to the correct instructions. It now points at the file that actually exists, so when the system synchronizes its data structure it will apply the intended changes instead of failing or skipping them. This is behind-the-scenes maintenance that does not change any feature you see, but it prevents the update process from tripping over itself. The fix is live today.

Previous implementation failed for arrays, causing valid tools to be incorrectly filtered out. Affects SDK run path. Added regression test in sdk/src/__tests__/run-mcp-tool-filter.test.ts.

eli5.text: When you run the assistant through the developer toolkit, it can now correctly pick which tools to use from a pre-approved list. Previously, a small coding mistake caused some valid tools to be silently ignored, so you might have noticed certain actions not working even though they were supposed to be available. This is live today, so tools in the approved list now work as expected.

ai.summary: isDeploymentHours in web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts now returns true unconditionally, removing the 10am - 8pm ET time window check. ai.title: Add dedicated load-skills test coverage
ai.summary: Adds `sdk/src/__tests__/load-skills.test.ts` to verify skill discovery logic. Tests cover default root scanning, explicit `skillsPath` overrides, precedence rules (project > global, .agents > .claude), and error handling for malformed or invalid skill definitions. Ensures `loadSkills` correctly filters directories by name constraints and frontmatter validity.

eli5.text: The system that finds and loads your custom instruction files now has a set of automated checks to make sure it keeps working correctly. These checks verify that it still looks in all the right spots (like your home folder and the project you're working on), follows the right override rules when duplicate instructions exist in multiple places, and gracefully skips broken or invalid files instead of crashing. This is a behind-the-scenes quality improvement for the development tools, you won't see a new feature, but it reduces the chance of surprises when the system reads your instruction files.
